sections.title: Checks the rules for creating Yard records
sections.what: Defines a sample source and three tests. The first confirms a problem signal naming no project is not applicable. The second confirms a problem's stage needs a supporting phrase in its own evidence, otherwise the project is held. The third confirms announcements keep their stage rules and that a blank project name is held.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are the rules that stop unsupported records being created in Yard.
sections.watch_out: The tests cover only the subject rules, so other sync steps have no checks in this file.

summary: Automatic checks for three rules that decide whether a signal may become a Yard record.
purpose: Protects against unsupported records being created in Yard.
why: Likely reason: guards against regressions in the no-guessing rules described in yardSync.ts.
how: 1. Loads Node's built-in test tools. 2. Builds a sample source. 3. Runs three tests: a problem signal naming no project is skipped; a problem's stage needs a supporting phrase in its own evidence or the project is held; an announcement keeps its stage rules, and a blank project name is held.
inputs: Sample signal records defined inside the file.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each of the three tests.
risks: Covers only the subject rules, not the country, linking or writing rules. A pass here does not prove the database writes are correct.
debug: Run the test file with Node's test runner. If a test fails, the failing check shows which rule changed; compare it with the rules in yardSync.ts.
